rationale:
bugs_open/390 follow-up, decided on a PRE-REGISTERED rule and a measured sample. Migration 635 renders the measured override_requirement into the css-patch prompt; when needs_important is false its block says 'Do NOT use !important - it is not needed to win here; this measured section supersedes the general !important guidance below.' Migration 616's general guidance ('mark ONLY the single property you are correcting as !important') sits ~19,700 chars later, near the prompt's end.

THE MEASURED BEHAVIOUR [2026-08-26, first day both were live together]: SIX of SIX attributed repairs across two sites kept !important against the block's explicit Do-NOT — remortgagecalculator.uk 9b2b2ce9 (llm_call_log 14:34:16 UTC: BEAT block rendered at char 137, Do-NOT at 577, and the reply still carried !important) and garden-tools.uk fd933538 + four more (5/5 of that site's attributed completions, counted from result.response.css_fix.result.css_added). Every one met the specificity requirement — the block IS being read — and every one disobeyed the one sentence that contradicts a later instruction. 'Supersedes the guidance below' adjudicated by the model is a comment, not a control (the estate's own rule, one level up).

THE CHANGE makes the contradiction UNREPRESENTABLE instead of adjudicated: (1) wrap 616's three bullets in {{if not .input_data.spec.override_requirement}}...{{end}} so they render ONLY when no measured requirement exists; (2) reword 635's else-sentence, whose 'guidance below' would otherwise dangle, to 'Do NOT use !important - it is not needed to win here: a selector meeting the requirement above wins without it.' Exactly one of the two instruction families can now render, proven by executing the post-apply template (extracted from the rehearsal transaction, NOT a hand copy) against five data shapes under the production parse (template.New('agent_prompt') + the datahelpers funcmap, default options): legacy, attributed+needs_important:false, attributed+needs_important:true, winning_rule-with-nil-requirement, unattributed. All render; the two families never co-occur.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS: needs_important:false is today an INERT signal — the filer computes it (cascadia, satisfiesRequirement) and the agent ignores it, so every attributed repair ships a redundant !important. Today that is harmless (the selector already wins). The day a repair must NOT use !important to avoid outranking a deliberate later rule, the signal has to actually gate — and a signal ignored six times out of six on day one will be ignored then too.

SEQUENCING, stated so the seats' checks read correctly: this migration will be APPLIED immediately after submission (config is live at once and tonight's repair batch is still draining), so read-only checks will observe the POST-apply world — has_old_sentence:false is my sequencing, not drift. Literals were sliced from the live row's prompt_template bytes by script, never retyped (616's twice-bitten lesson); guard and edit share one DO block with each literal declared once; row-count assertion before read and GET DIAGNOSTICS after write (616 round-2's HIGH objection, kept); drift guards anchor on exactly-once presence of the 616 passage and 635's own fence. Drift anchor for future prompt migrations is now THIS file's shape.

Template proof on the EXTRACTED post-apply artefact under production semantics (datahelpers.RenderPromptTemplate: template.New('agent_prompt').Funcs(toJSON/placeholder/rangeStart/rangeEnd), default options, data_helpers.go:1129-1152): five shapes ALL PASS, general/doNot/must flags exclusive in every render.

platform/orchestration/actions/write_render_audit_findings_action.go + contrast_cascade_route.go: needs_important is computed by the filer (cascadia + satisfiesRequirement); nothing else consumes it - the prompt is its only reader, which is why an ignored rendering makes it fully inert.
plan.risks:
1) EXPECTED OBJECTION - 'the redundant !important is harmless, why spend a round?' Harmless to today's pixel, yes; but needs_important:false is one of the three fields the whole attribution pipeline exists to compute, and it is being overridden by a stale general instruction 6/6 times. The fence costs two string operations and restores the signal's meaning.
2) THE REAL BEHAVIOURAL CHANGE: attributed repairs will now ship WITHOUT !important (when needs_important is false). They still win - the platform VERIFIED the override_example satisfies the requirement before writing it - but if the verification were ever wrong, the !important was masking it. That masking is exactly what P3 (retraction at the next audit) exists to catch, and the first no-!important repairs will be graded there. If a strictly-greater selector somehow fails to take, the design wants to SEE that, not have it papered over.
3) Legacy/unattributed rows are byte-identical in behaviour: the fence only ever REMOVES text when a requirement exists; shapes with no override_requirement render exactly today's prompt (proof shapes 1, 4, 5).
4) Mid-batch apply: tonight's remaining rows will render the new prompt mid-drain. Intended - but it splits tonight's sample into before/after, so the NOTES record which rows rendered which prompt by llm_call_log timestamp.
5) A future migration anchoring on 635's block text will now miss - the drift anchor moves to 655's shape, stated in the file header and the lane handoff.
